policy: Primary papers and official project documentation only. Abstract-only or inaccessible materials are not used for a new theorem.

sources.title: Reading Rational Univariate Representations on lexicographic Groebner bases
sources.read_scope: Abstract, introduction, Section 2, Theorem 1 and separation discussion in the full primary text.
sources.conditions: A zero-dimensional ideal over a field; the proofs assume characteristic zero or sufficiently large characteristic where needed. A separating form must be certified for an actual RUR. Shape position is not assumed in the general algorithm.
sources.used_for: Determine why the fixed-J rational surface is not yet an eligible finite RUR input; design a finite divisor-domain elimination before seeking an empty-root certificate.
sources.not_claimed: No integer-point finiteness theorem, installation of the authors' software, or RUR execution is claimed. Our small-prime Bezout certificates are verified directly rather than by invoking the paper in small characteristic.

sources.title: RationalUnivariateRepresentation.jl official documentation
sources.conditions: Zero-dimensional polynomial systems over the rationals or a prime field; radical parametrization, optional separating-form and multiplicity information.

sources.title: New efficient algorithms for computing Groebner bases of saturation ideals (F4SAT) and colon ideals (Sparse-FGLM-colon)
sources.read_scope: Introduction and algebraic setup in the primary full text.
sources.conditions: Polynomial ideal I and polynomial phi over a field. Saturation is (I + <1-t*phi>) intersected with the original polynomial ring. Its variety is the Zariski closure of the open set difference; finiteness does not follow merely from saturation.
sources.used_for: Rabinowitsch saturation by w*n*(n-1), with nonzero and integer conditions retained separately.
sources.not_claimed: The F4SAT or Sparse-FGLM-colon implementation was not run.
